label: SB-19 overload/recovery: 2x saturation then back to normal, goodput/rejections/recovery time (contract section 3.7)
methodology: server cells only, unary 1 KiB, fixed native open-loop Poisson generator. Per repeat: (1) geometric saturation search from search_start_rate until the first rate the server cannot sustain (saturation_rate; the last clean rate is normal_rate; the firing signal is recorded per repeat). The knee signal is server errors/timeouts, or rejections persisting at the escalated cap: a bounded generator sheds load before a slowing server ever errors, so rejection persistence within a fixed concurrency budget is the observable knee. Rejected steps escalate --max-in-flight once (clean after escalation means the cap was too small: keep climbing); CPU-saturated steps invalidate as inconclusive; (2) a baseline probe at normal_rate, stepping normal down (bounded, recorded) until it reproduces clean; (3) one overload phase at overload_factor x saturation_rate reporting goodput, error/timeout/rejection rates and p99 with retained failures (rejections are a reported result, not an invalidator); (4) short recovery probes at normal_rate until clean (zero errors, p99 within recovery_p99_factor of baseline, generator uncapped) or the probe budget exhausts. Overload is a validation axis, not a gate: pass means every probe reconciles (offered == successful + failed + rejected), no probe is generator-capped except the overload phase's reported rejections, and recovery is measured and reported either way. Dropped or misclassified failures invalidate the run (contract 3.7). Gating uses the SB-11 client-CPU saturation signal plus rejections; the contract 4.1 lag rule is recorded per probe for auditors. Streaming-shape overload stays future work. Cell order is frozen: peers in file order.
goodput_formula: goodput_mib_s = successful_rpcs x app_bytes_per_rpc / (duration_s x 1048576); unary app_bytes_per_rpc = req_bytes + resp_bytes (application payload, framing excluded, contract 5.3). Streaming shapes (future): msgs x per-message app bytes per direction summed per the shape.
